text:
sam: heads up — onboarding sample for Bun is failing for a customer. crash happens during import + auth refresh. stack is messy, looks like ESM export resolution + body stream reuse problem. anyone familiar with our bun/deno story?
erin: hmm, do you have the exact error? Bun usually complains about conditional exports if package.json doesn't have an explicit "bun" or ESM entry.
sam: error: \"Uncaught Error: Cannot find module 'redwood-inference'\" in bun runtime. then when I force import the dist/esm bundle via URL, calls that trigger token refresh result in two POSTs to the backend.
chris: two POSTs = classic retry + body consumed. browsers have Request.clone(), node-fetch has clone() too, but Bun's Request body is a stream that might not support cloning. we probably assume clone in retry layer.
maya: do we stream bodies for generation calls in the sample? sample-app sends small JSON, so cloning is easy (read body text and reuse), but our SDK tries to be generic.
sam: minimal repro in sample:
```ts
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('RW_KEY') })
await c.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
```
using bun v1.22, fails on import. using URL import of /dist/esm/index.mjs works but then auth retry triggers second request with no Authorization header (backend rejects first then accepts second).
erin: sounds like two problems: 1) packaging exports for Bun/Deno, 2) retry middleware failing to preserve headers/body across retries.
chris: for (1) we can add a conditional export in package.json: "exports": { "./deno": "./dist/deno.mjs", "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } — that should help bundlers and Bun. also optionally provide types: "types/deno.d.ts".
maya: for (2) implementation idea: use a small util that normalizes a Request-like input into {url, init} where init has headers as a Headers instance and body as a reusable Uint8Array when possible. Pseudocode:
```js
async function normalize(req){
  const url = req.url || req
  const init = {}
  init.method = req.method
  init.headers = new Headers(req.headers || {})
  if (req.body) {
    const buf = await readAll(req.body)
    init.body = buf
  }
  return {url, init}
}
```
This avoids relying on Request.clone in runtimes that don't support it.
ron: small gotcha: in Deno some Request.body is a ReadableStream not a Node stream. readAll needs to handle both. add a simple runtime detector.
sam: would this preserve Authorization? I saw the retried request arrived without auth header.
chris: that'd fix it: the bug is we were reconstructing headers from a plain object and accidentally dropped header keys with lowercase/uppercase mismatches. Using Headers normalizes and keeps get()/set() semantics.
erin: typing and DX note: TypeScript users got confused because our README showed `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` but our ESM export is named. change docs to `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference/deno'` (once we add deno entry) and publish deno.d.ts that re-exports correct types.
maya: CI trap: sample-app-deno in CI used node-targeted bundle which masked the bug. sdk-bot: CI: sample-app-deno job failed on linux/bun image https://ci.internal/infra/issue/9988 (flaky).
ron: plan: (a) add deno/bun build artifact (dist/deno.mjs + dist/bun.mjs) in release pipeline (b) fix retry to use normalize util for headers/body (c) update package.json exports and add types/deno.d.ts (d) update sample quickstart + add a BUN/DENO section in README with exact import + minimal polyfills if needed.
sam: I'll open a PR for the sample change and a small repro harness that runs in bun docker. assign reviewers @chris @maya.
erin: i'll own the package.json export updates and coordinate release steps.
chris: I'll implement the normalize util and add tests for retry behavior across node/deno/bun. also add a tiny fallback where if body is a stream we buffer up to N bytes and error if over limit to avoid huge mem usage.
maya: nice. UX request: add a one-liner code snippet in quickstart for people who just want everything to work in Deno: `import {RedwoodClient} from 'redwood-inference/deno'` then `globalThis.fetch ||= (...args) => fetch(...args)` — short and explicit.
sam: thanks all. pinged in PR with the CI link. will update thread with PR numbers. :thumbsup:
